test_title: PYST 47: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 24 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Dandi March of 1930?

(a)The march started from Sabarmati Ashram and ended at Dandi, covering a distance of 240 miles.

(b) The Dandi March led to the signing of the Poona Pact
solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Dandi March was a non-violent protest led by Mahatma Gandhi as part of the Civil Disobedience Movement.
 
• The march began on 12th March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram near Ahmedabad and ended at Dandi, a coastal village in Gujarat, covering a distance of 241 miles.
 
• The primary objective of the march was to protest against the British salt monopoly and the imposition of tax on salt.
 
• The Dandi March is considered a pivotal event in India's struggle for independence as it mobilized mass participation.
 
• Statement (b) regarding the Poona Pact is incorrect because the Poona Pact was signed in 1932, unrelated to the Dandi March.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Civil Disobedience Movement:**

 
 
• Launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930 as a non-violent campaign against British rule.
 
• Focused on breaking unjust laws, such as the salt tax, and boycotting British goods and institutions.
 
• The movement significantly contributed to raising national consciousness and mass participation.
 
 
 
• **Salt Tax:**
 
 
• Imposed by the British colonial government, forcing Indians to purchase salt from British-controlled sources.
 
• Seen as exploitative and symbolized the broader economic injustices of colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Poona Pact:**
 
 
• An agreement signed in 1932 between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar regarding the reservation of seats for depressed classes in the legislature.
 
• It is unrelated to the Dandi March and occurred two years later.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Dandi March:**
 
 
• Inspired civil disobedience campaigns across India against various colonial laws.
 
• Highlighted the power of non-violent protest in challenging oppressive regimes.
